articles.headline: 'Never say never!' Bruno Fernandes leaves door wide open for sensational Sporting homecoming after Lisbon brace
keyFacts: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes stated he will never close the door on returning to play for Sporting CP in the future.
Fernandes scored two goals and muted his celebrations during Manchester United's 2-2 Champions League draw against his former club, Sporting CP.
Ahead of Sporting's match against Porto, Fernandes advised his former team to maintain the unity that helped them contend for titles.
body: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Bruno Fernandes admitted he would never close the door on returning to Sporting CP after receiving a special pre-match tribute and scoring twice in Manchester United's 2-2 Champions League draw. The United captain also explained why he muted his celebrations and shared title advice ahead of Sporting's clash with FC Porto.
Fernandes leaves the door open for a Sporting homecoming

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes insisted he will never close the door on playing for Sporting CP again after marking his first return to the Jose Alvalade Stadium in almost seven years with two goals in Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw. Honoured prior to kick-off with a framed number-eight memento presented by club president Frederico Varandas, the Portuguese midfielder spoke warmly about his enduring bond with the Lions.

"The door has never been closed. I have enormous affection for the club. That possibility depends on many people. I'm not closing that door, I never will. I've been happy here and I can be again, if that happens," Fernandes told Sport TV after full-time .
Explaining his muted celebrations after quickfire brace

Having scored 64 goals in 137 appearances for Sporting between January 2017 and January 2020 before joining United, Fernandes kept his celebrations restrained when his 48th-minute penalty and a bobbling 50th-minute strike briefly put the visitors 2-1 ahead.

"The goal was strange, it took me a while to realise the ball had gone in. But that's how I felt at that moment," he explained. "I don't think a player has more or less respect for not celebrating a goal, but I ended up not celebrating it as enthusiastically."
Backing Sporting ahead of crucial O Classico clash

While United saw Diogo Dalot—a former FC Porto academy graduate who beat Sporting at the Dragao in 2018—heavily booed upon his 64th-minute introduction, Fernandes offered encouragement to his former club ahead of Monday's Primeira Liga showdown against unbeaten leaders Porto.

"I think what Sporting needs most is the unity it has had in recent years, which allowed it to come close to being champion or even winning the title. This was noticeable, especially in the final minutes, and it must continue like this," Fernandes said. "I see a team with a lot of quality and a very complete squad. I hope Sporting fights for the title until the end."
Sporting brace for title test at Estadio do Dragao
Sporting sit third in the Primeira Liga on 24 points—nine behind a Porto side boasting 11 wins from 11 league matches—heading into Monday's trip to Estadio do Dragao.
Although Porto have dominated domestically, five of the last six league meetings between the rivals in Porto have ended in draws, giving Sporting hope as they chase a vital title-race boost.

articles.headline: Colorado State blows 27-point halftime lead before McIver tops Clemson with last-second bucket 77-75
keyFacts: Colorado State defeated Clemson 77-75 in the Maui Invitational after blowing a 27-point halftime lead.
Jojo McIver scored the game-winning basket for Colorado State at the buzzer to secure the victory.
Clemson will play at home against Auburn on Tuesday and Colorado State will host UT Arlington.
body: LAHAINA, Hawaii (AP) — Jojo McIver scored his only points of the game at the buzzer to give Colorado State a 77-75 win over Clemson after the Rams had blown a 27-point halftime lead in the seventh-place contest of the Maui Invitational on Wednesday night.
McIver drove from the right baseline and dropped in a left-handed shot to avoid what could have been a near-record collapse.

On Dec. 30, 1950, Duke overcame a 29-point halftime deficit to beat Tulane 74-72 — the largest Division I halftime deficit overcome for a win. It looked like Clemson (4-4) might pull off its own monumental comeback after scoring the first 18 points of the second half to cut CSU's 55-28 halftime lead to single digits. The Tigers' surge continued until they took their first lead since 4-2 on a David Fuchs free throw to make it 66-65 with five minutes left.
The game was tied with a minute to go. A Clemson challenge on an out-of-bounds call gave the Tigers the ball with 42.8 seconds left but Fuchs missed a 3-pointer and McIver converted at the other end.

Pops Dunson scored all 16 of his points in the first half when the Rams (5-3) made 14 straight baskets, including nine 3s, and shot 69% to Clemson's 23%. But in the second half it was Clemson shooting 63% and Colorado State 29%. Josh Pascarelli also scored 16 for CSU.
Fuchs and Chase Thompson scored 19 apiece for Clemson.
The Tigers were without 6-foot-9 starter Liutauras Lelevicius after a lower leg injury suffered in Tuesday’s 64-63 loss to Washington.
Colorado State was coming off an 84-81 loss on Tuesday when VCU made a 45-footer.
Up next
Clemson: Home against Auburn on Tuesday.
Colorado State: Home against UT Arlington on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI in war
keyFacts: Iranian officials criticized U.S. military AI use and accused Israel of using false chemical weapons claims to drag the U.S. into war.
Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi ports and Riyadh after Saudi coalition strikes hit the Houthi-controlled Red Sea port of Hodeidah.
Iran claimed to tighten control over the Strait of Hormuz following reported ship explosions, despite an ongoing U.S. naval blockade.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:
- Iran's U.N. ambassador on Tuesday criticized the U.S. military's use of in the nearly 9-month war, claiming American forces leveraged the technology to plan and over just four days.
- The Iran-backed Houthi group claimed an attack on the financial district of Saudi Arabia's capital on Wednesday, as well on a sprawling oil refinery in the country's east.
- Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Iran is developing chemical weapons and vowed to stop Tehran from obtaining them. has repeatedly denied it is developing chemical weapons.
U.K. navy monitor says tanker off UAE reported nearby explosion, sustained no damage

The U.K. navy's Maritime Trade Operations agency said late Wednesday that it had received a report of an explosion near a tanker about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai, in the United Arab Emirates, west of the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.
The tanker's master reported an explosion, which UKMTO attributed to an "unknown projectile," but the vessel was not damaged and there was no environmental impact, UKMTO said in an advisory.

Iran claimed earlier Wednesday, without offering evidence or details, that a liquified natural gas carrier had struck a sea mine in the southern part of the strait — the latest in a series of similar daily claims.

Iran insists all vessels must use northern shipping lanes through the strait, and only with authorization from its military. The regime said Wednesday that it was tightening its control over the vital waterway, which the U.S. military insists is safe and open to traffic.
Houthis claim attacks on Saudi ports

Yemen's Houthis said Wednesday they had targeted the Saudi ports of Jeddah and Jazan in response to Saudi strikes on a Yemeni port controlled by the Iran-backed group as their conflict further escalated.
The attacks came after the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said it had struck Yemen's Red Sea port city of Hodeida, drawing threats of retaliation from the Yemeni fighters.
"Both operations resulted in damage to the targeted sites," Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said.

An explosion was later heard in Saudi capital Riyadh, according to an AFP journalist and residents, after authorities issued an alert warning of a "hostile aerial threat," which was lifted shortly after.
Residents in northern and eastern Riyadh confirmed hearing the blast, with one saying their house windows "shook violently."

Saudi forces said air defenses destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward the capital by the Houthis, as well as a cruise missile in the western part of the country and a drone near Jeddah's port.
Turki al-Malki, the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition battling the Houthis, said no civilian injuries resulted from the debris of the intercepted drone.
In recent weeks, the Houthis has launched a barrage at Saudi targets including the financial district, airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.

The Saudi coalition has in turn been striking Houthi-held areas of Yemen in support of the internationally-recognized government, which has been battling the Houthis for territory since a civil war reignited in July.
CBS/AFP
Iran criticizes Sen. Cornyn for incorrectly citing nuclear report actually about North Korea

The Iranian Foreign Ministry has called out Republican Sen. John Cornyn for a post on X criticizing Iran's alleged pursuit of nuclear weapons, however, the quote cited by the senator was actually about North Korean nuclear ambitions.
The Texas senator cited International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi raising concern "about a rapidly built extension at the Yongbyon gas centrifuge uranium enrichment plant."
Cornyn wrote on X, "Doesn't sound like the Iranian regime is giving up on its nuclear weapons aspirations."
Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei correctly pointed out Grossi was speaking about Yongbyon, North Korea, and nothing to do with Iran.

Cornyn serves on the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, one of the governing body's most important posts. Cornyn is on his way out of the Senate. He was soundly defeated by Ken Paxton in the Republican primary this spring. Paxton would eventually lose earlier this month to Democrat James Talarico.
The post on X remains live 24 hours after the senator shared it.
Israel trying to deceive U.S. into war with chemical weapons claim, Iran says
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Israel was trying to drag the United States into another war after an Israeli minister alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons.

"This warmonger shamelessly accuses Iran ... of developing and concealing such heinous weapons in pharmaceutical factories. The objective is audacious: to deceive the US into fighting yet another war on its behalf," he wrote in a statement posted on X.

Israel has for years accused Iran of trying to acquire nuclear weapons, but Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz on Tuesday alleged Tehran is building chemical weapons and vowed to stop the Islamic republic from obtaining them.

"Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons but has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them," said Katz in a statement published by his Likud party on Telegram. He also left open the possibility of preemptive strikes against Iran.
"We must not allow this to proceed," he said.

President Trump mentioned the same thing to Fox News earlier this month on his Asia trip, saying, "Well, there is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear. ... Nuclear is much harder, and they're looking at gas and they're looking at the bio, the biological weapons."
CBS/AFP
Houthi projectile hits Saudi Arabia's Jazan port, causing minor damage
A projectile fired by the Houthi militia struck Jazan port in southwestern Saudi Arabia, causing minor damage but no civilian casualties, the Saudi-led coalition said on Wednesday.
It said efforts were underway to determine the type of projectile.

The Iran-backed Houthis reiterated earlier on Wednesday their threat to target Jeddah and all Saudi Arabian ports on the Red Sea if Saudi Arabia followed through on its threat to target Yemen's Hodeidah port, which is held by the rebels.
Hodeidah is the main entry point for food and other essential supplies into Houthi-held northern Yemen.
Shortly after the Houthis' warning, the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV network reported a Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah.
Iran claims natural gas tanker struck sea mine in Strait of Hormuz, causing an explosion

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed Wednesday that a liquified natural gas carrier exploded after striking a sea mine while transiting what it calls an unauthorized route through the southern Strait of Hormuz — shipping lanes the and safe for travel.

The IRGC statement, carried Wednesday by state television network IRIB and other Iranian media, did not provide any further information about the ship purportedly impacted, and there was no immediate report from independent monitoring agencies of a vessel being hit Wednesday.

Iran has repeatedly warned vessels not to ignore its restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, saying ships must only use northern shipping lanes through the waterway, close to its shores, and only with authorization from Iranian authorities.
The IRGC said Wednesday that ships being "deceived by the plundering U.S. military" were at risk of striking naval mines.
Iranian army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said Wednesday that Iran's forces had tightened their control over and monitoring of the Strait of Hormuz.
U.S. Treasury chief calls Iranian regime a sinking ship
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that the Iranian regime was a "sinking ship."

In a brief social media post, Bessent said Iran had failed to load a single oil tanker since the Treasury in August, which he called at the time an "unprecedented campaign against the Islamic Republic of Iran and its enablers."

The initiative is aimed at using economic tools - including secondary sanctions against countries and entities that do business with Iran - to force the regime to halt its threats to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and to end the war.
While neither of those objectives has been met, Bessent said in his post on Wednesday that "Iran doesn't have a drop of oil on the water left to sell."
Iran dismisses U.S. naval blockade, claims boost in exports via "northern and other non-southern borders"

Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said Wednesday that Tehran is not concerned about the U.S.-imposed naval blockade of Iranian ports, claiming an increase in exports and the clearance of goods via other routes, according to state news agency IRNA.
Aref was quoted as saying increased commerce across Iran's "northern and other non-southern borders" demonstrated the Islamic Republic's ability to maintain supplies despite maritime restrictions.

The U.S. military announced earlier this month an expansion of its naval blockade, as Central Command heralded a new task force aimed at disrupting the illegal shipment of prohibited items such as military technology or illegal revenue streams over ground transportation routes into and out of Iran.

"The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper said in Nov. 7 a statement. "Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with U.S. interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military."

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Monday that a land blockade of Iran would be "almost impossible" given the country's vast territory, numerous provinces and extensive ties with neighboring countries.
U.K. reportedly taking extra precautions to protect warplanes on bases due to drone threat

Britain's air force is moving planes into hangars and hardened shelters overnight to protect them from drone threats, The Times and Sky News reported Wednesday. The two U.K. media outlets also said the Royal Air Force (RAF) is planning to install anti-drone nets around warplanes that remain exposed.

The Ministry of Defense did not immediately confirm the reports, but British authorities have issued warnings recently about the rising threats posed by Russia and Iran, and the government has urged citizens to that could make access to fresh food, water and other essentials difficult for days.
In October, the head of Britain's domestic spy agency MI5 warned that in its efforts to attack the U.K., including going after harder targets such as military bases,

He spoke weeks after authorities thwarted an alleged Iran-backed plot targeting the. That incident, for which with serious national security offenses, led the U.S. to , which had been used in strikes on Iran, from the base.
CBS/AFP
Houthis renew threat to target Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports

The Iran-backed Houthis reiterated on Wednesday their threat to target Jeddah and all Saudi Arabian ports on the Red Sea if the Saudis follow through on their threat to target Yemen's Hodeidah port, which is held by the rebels.
Hodeidah is the main entry point for food and other essential supplies into Houthi-held northern Yemen.

In a statement posted online, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree called on "employees and workers at these ports, as well as those present in their vicinity, to evacuate them immediately and move away."
Shortly after Saree issued the warning, the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV network reported a Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah.
The rebel group said earlier Wednesday that it had carried out two operations targeting the Ras Tanura refinery in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, as well as the financial center in Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense agency said Tuesday that a skyscraper in the financial district had been targeted by a Houthi attack, injuring 11 people.
U.N. humanitarian chief: Half of Yemen's population needs aid as "renewed fighting" drives displacement

United Nations humanitarian relief chief Tom Fletcher said Wednesday that half of Yemen's population is in need of aid, as he arrived in the war-torn nation that has become the most active front in the intertwined Middle East conflicts.
Fletcher warned in a statement shared online that "renewed fighting has forced over 364,000 people from their homes since August, including tens of thousands this past week alone."

He repeated his demand for Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels to "immediately and unconditionally release " and other humanitarian workers and said the U.N.-led relief efforts in the country were overstretched, underfunded and under attack.

"Yemen is where we are furthest off track on our ambition to reach 87 million people with lifesaving support this year," Fletcher said. "We will not allow the people of Yemen to slip off the world's radar."
Iran claims it has tightened its control over Strait of Hormuz
Iranian army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said the military had tightened its control and monitoring of the Strait of Hormuz on the orders of the army's commander-in-chief.

Ships attempting to transit the waterway without coordinating with Iran's armed forces have faced greater risks in recent weeks, including sea mines, Akraminia was quoted as saying Wednesday by the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

President Trump has dismissed Iran's claims attacks on ships and sea mines being laid in the strait as lies intended to inflate global energy prices, and the U.S. military international shipping lanes through the waterway free of mines at the end of October.

Without offering any evidence, however, Akraminia claimed Iranian forces had upgraded their monitoring capabilities by introducing new systems, improving existing ones and strengthening their combat abilities, and he said the measures would continue.

Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) said Tuesday that 26 tugboats had been added to the country's "Non-Compliance List," for providing services to non-compliant vessels, indicating they could be targeted.

Iran issues daily claims of commercial vessels striking mines in and near the strait, few of which are ever corroborated, but independent monitors do involving "unknown projectiles" striking ships in the region.
Iran criticizes U.S. for using artificial intelligence for deadly attacks
Iran has denounced the U.S. military's use of to plan and carry out attacks.
Speaking at a U.N. Security Council meeting Tuesday, Iranian Ambassador Gholamhossein Darzi said the weaponization of AI "raises serious concerns."

Darzi claimed U.S. forces used the technology to deploy more than 2,000 munitions to hit 2,000 distinct targets within 96 hours. He said Palantir's Maven and Anthropic's system were used to analyze intelligence, identify and prioritize targets and provide strike coordinates.

"Neither advanced technology nor the involvement of private companies can shield the United States or the Israeli regime from accountability for flagrant violations of their obligations under international law," Darzi told the council meeting.

"Those responsible for the commission of atrocious crimes against Iranian people, including deliberate attacks against civilians and civilian objects, must face individual criminal accountability," he added.

In March 2026, the Commander of U.S. Central Command Adm. Brad Cooper confirmed American forces had used a "variety of advanced AI tools" in order to "cut through the noise and make smarter decisions faster than the enemy can react."
While the Pentagon has not said exactly how AI tools are being deployed, CBS News spoke in March with several experts with knowledge of military operations who described the likely scenarios.

"The military is now processing roughly a thousand potential targets a day and striking the majority of them, with turnaround time for the next strike potentially under four hours," said retired Navy Admiral Mark Montgomery, senior director of the Foundation for Defense of Democracy's Center on Cyber and Technology Innovation. "A human is still in the loop, but AI is doing the work that used to take days of analysis — and doing it at a scale no previous campaign has matched."
Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi forces intensify attacks

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".
In separate attacks, Saudi's forces said they had struck the city of Hodeida on Wednesday, after the Houthis said they would retaliate if that attack took place.

The Houthis have been locked in grueling, more than decade-long civil war against Yemen's government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia. Recent Houthi gains have consolidated the group's control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which the group has tried to use to disrupt Saudi oil exports.
CBS/AFP
Iran developing chemical weapons, Israeli defense minister says, warns of possible preemptive strike
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday that Iran is developing chemical weapons, and vowed to stop Tehran from obtaining them.

"Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons," Katz said in a briefing to Israeli reporters, according to public broadcaster KAN and other national outlets. "The state of Israel will not allow them to reach that capability."
In his briefing on Tuesday, Katz floated the possibility of a preemptive strike against Tehran, if necessary.

"If we recognize that the Iranians intend to attack Israel, can't we tell the army to attack earlier and thwart the threat?" he said, according to a transcript from Israel's Channel 12. "If the Iranians attack us first, it will be a failure."

Katz's comments came at the same time as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi criticized the U.S. government for not funding the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, the international body that monitors and combats chemical weapons use at The Hague. The organization is facing a budget crisis because the U.S. has pulled funding, according to a Reuters report.

"The U.S. is so concerned about chemical arms that it's crippling the world's chemical weapons watchdog," Araghchi wrote Tuesday on X. "OPCW may be forced to suspend work and scale back vital programs. By obstructing its mandate, the U.S. is deliberately putting global peace and security at risk. Shameful."
The OPCW won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013 for its work in Syria.
CBS/AFP
Jury convicts Chinese tech giant Huawei over business with Iran, other conspiracy charges
A U.S. jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies on Tuesday of conspiring to steal trade secrets and doing business in countries subject to U.S. sanctions, including Iran.

In all, Huawei was convicted on 10 of 12 counts. The case in Brooklyn federal court involved no human defendants, but the company could be made to pay billions of dollars in penalties when it is sentenced next September.

The Department of Justice said Huawei and its subsidiaries assisted an Iranian intelligence apparatus called Zaeim in monitoring and censoring internet access. The company also provided surveillance cameras that helped Tehran monitor protest activity, according to the DOJ.

"Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the U.S. government that it did not assist Iran's government, military, or intelligence community; that it began restricting its business in Iran in 2011; that Skycom was a business partner, rather than a wholly-owned subsidiary; and that Huawei complied with all applicable sanctions," the DOJ said. "Huawei knew that all of those statements were materially false and misleading."
CBS/AP

articles.headline: FedEx plane overshoots runway at Miami airport on Thanksgiving eve
keyFacts: A FedEx cargo plane overran a runway during heavy rain at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night with no reported injuries.
The incident closed most runways and caused multi-hour delays during the Thanksgiving travel rush, officials reported.
The Federal Aviation Administration launched an investigation, and the airport advised passengers to check airline statuses before traveling.
body: A FedEx cargo plane went past the end of a runway at Miami International Airport on Wednesday night, shutting most of the airport's runways as the Thanksgiving travel rush began in the United States.
It forced the closure of all but one runway, and by early Thursday the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was reporting delays of several hours.
The aircraft was a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 arriving from Memphis. The FAA has launched an investigation.
What happened to the plane?
The airport said the plane overran Runway 26R at about 8:40 pm local time.
FedEx said the plane had "an issue upon landing" and that it is working with investigators. "We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries," the company said.
The incident happened amid heavy rain. No injuries were reported.
The airport advised passengers to check with their airlines before traveling.
Overrunning the runway at Miami airport
It is the second runway overrun at Miami in under three months. An Amazon cargo jet overshot a different runway in September, crossing a road and hitting a van and killing five people on the ground.

Three of the airport's runways meet at their western end, so the FedEx plane came to rest near where the Amazon jet went off. A minor collision also occurred between a Copa planand a UPS plane on a taxiway less than two weeks ago.
FedEx only resumed MD-11 flights in May. The type was grounded after a UPS MD-11 crashed in Kentucky last year, killing three pilots and 12 people on the ground.
The incident is the latest in a rough stretch for US aviation, including a nationwide halt to takeoffs on November 13 over air traffic control communication problems.
Up to 80 million people are traveling for Thanksgiving in the country, with a storm expected in the northeastern US.

articles.headline: Four-time MVP Rodgers released and may have played last NFL game
keyFacts: The Pittsburgh Steelers released four-time MVP quarterback Aaron Rodgers following tension with head coach Mike McCarthy and his replacement as the starter.
Rodgers stated on a sports talk show that he would not rejoin the team, and head coach Mike McCarthy cited an ultimatum as the reason for his release.
Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback for the Steelers against the Denver Broncos, while Rodgers is now free to sign with another team.
body: - Published
Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers.
In a brief statement published on Wednesday afternoon local time, the Steelers announced Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, was no longer with the franchise.
That came after a tumultuous 24 hours, which began with the Steelers announcing at 23:10 local time on Tuesday that Rodgers had been replaced as their starting quarterback.
He then appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, saying he would not rejoin the team.
"That ship has sailed," said Rodgers, who turns 43 next week.
During the 34-minute interview, he was critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings.

They won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2011 and, during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers claims that McCarthy ended the half-time huddle with a chant of "one, two, three, Packers".
McCarthy, 63, was in charge for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell with the Packers and left in 2018. He then coached the Dallas Cowboys from 2020-2024.
Tension had developed between the pair over play-calling and Rodgers says he told McCarthy "try to bench me or don't change the play-caller, then you should just release me".

Shortly before Pittsburgh confirmed his release, McCarthy responded to Rodgers' interview, telling reporters "there was an ultimatum made that was clearly outside his job description", adding it was his decision to let the player go.
All this came after the Steelers said that Mason Rudolph will start Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos and that Rodgers would be inactive, so would not serve as back-up to the 31-year-old.
Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets, was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs.
McCarthy's appointment persuaded him to play one more year but Rodgers told the talk show on Wednesday the season had not been "what I signed up for".
Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have had two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at Philadelphia on Sunday.
Analysis - an unceremonious end to an illustrious career?
Pittsburgh's brief statement confirming Rodgers' release, external is likely the unceremonious end to an illustrious career.
While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win with Green Bay, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times.
Rodgers had said his 22nd year in the NFL would be his last, and he has been let go at a crucial stage in the season.
The Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) lead the AFC North division, with Pittsburgh third, but with seven games left the Steelers occupy the final play-off spot for the AFC Conference.
Although Pittsburgh are 6-4, they have had to grind out some of those wins as they have struggled offensively. They rank 22nd for both points and passing yards per game.
Rodgers is undoubtedly past his best, but his form has only dropped slightly from last season and the team's struggles are by no means entirely down to him.

The Steelers' depth among their wide receivers is thin. Michael Pittman is out injured and DK Metcalf has not delivered the production expected when he was brought in with Rodgers before the 2025 season.
Metcalf, 28, was even ejected during Sunday's loss at Philadelphia, meaning Rodgers had to lean on debutant Max Hurleman with the game on the line.
It is not as if Pittsburgh had a hot-shot rookie quarterback pushing for an opportunity. Rudolph is in his ninth season and has started each as a back-up.

But this week's discussions with Rodgers forced McCarthy's hand and the manner in which the situation unraveled cannot be a complete surprise given Rodgers has clashed with team management, coaches and team-mates throughout his career.
While McCarthy hopes Rudolph can spark the Steelers' offence, Rodgers is now free to join another team.

Several have had quarterback issues this season through injuries and poor form, and with more than a third of it left, there is time for Rodgers - one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time - to come aboard and make an impact.
The Indianapolis Colts are one of those teams having released Daniel Jones last week, but they are out of play-off contention.
That leaves the New England Patriots as an intriguing alternative.
Drake Maye will be out for at least six weeks after suffering a fractured fibula and at 5-5 are just outside the AFC's play-off spots - one below Pittsburgh.
The Patriots have Super Bowl pedigree having reached last season's big game and Rodgers would relish the chance to deny McCarthy and his former team.
It would also give him the opportunity to follow his former adversary Tom Brady and get one last shot at finally emulating Brady and Manning by becoming a multiple Super Bowl winner himself.

body: In Pictures
Women have rallied around the world to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.
About 47,000 women and girls were intentionally killed by an intimate partner or family member last year, according to data from the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and UN Women.
The figures, published on Tuesday in the 2026 Femicide Brief to coincide with the international day, show the scale of gender-based killings worldwide.
While the 47,000 figure is lower than the 2024 estimate of 50,000 victims, the UN said this change largely reflects improved country-level data rather than an actual decrease in femicides.
No region was spared, with such killings recorded across the globe. The UN found that while overall homicide rates have declined worldwide, femicide rates have fallen at a slower pace.

articles.headline: Neuralink receives FDA approval for 'pivotal' brain implant trial in ALS patients
keyFacts: Neuralink announced that it received FDA approval to launch its first pivotal trial for the LINK brain-computer interface in ALS patients.
The study will evaluate the safety, reliability, and effectiveness of allowing paralyzed patients to control digital devices using thoughts alone.
Neuralink now has approval to recruit participants and conduct the study, which could lead to future market release applications if proven safe.
body: Neuralink receives FDA approval for 'pivotal' brain implant trial in ALS patients
The study will evaluate the efficacity and safety of the company’s LINK device.

Elon Musk's Neuralink has received FDA permission to launch the first "pivotal" trial for its implantable LINK brain-computer interface, the company announced. The study represents a more advanced step in the company's efforts to develop a brain implant that allows people with paralysis to control devices using their brain alone. It will be open to a limited number of patients with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that damages nerve cells controlling voluntary muscle movement.

"We've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US," Neuralink announced on X. "This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date."

Neuralink hit a milestone last year when the company revealed that its first participant with ALS named Bradford Smith was able to communicate using brain signals alone. "Neuralink has given me freedom, hope, and faster communication. ... It has improved my life so much. I'm so happy to be involved in something big that will help many people," Smith said at the time.
We've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US. This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date.
Those with ALS may be eligible. To learn more:https://t.co/dWhb5N4GdR pic.twitter.com/Vor7iXXCBA
— Neuralink (@neuralink) November 25, 2026

The FDA authorization was granted on an experimental basis, but it's a key step forward for Neuralink's LINK brain-implant system. The study will evaluate the ability of patients to control digital devices through thought, "with a focus on functional outcomes that improve independence in daily life," Neuralink wrote. It will also assess the system's long-term safety and reliability.

WIth Neuralink's latest system, the company's N1 implant is surgically placed in the skull, then the company uses its R1 robot to insert flexible electrodes into the brain. Neural activity from the brain associated with movement is then interpreted by software, which translates signals into commands for controlling computers or digital devices. The technology is designed to help patients communicate with the outside world, with the eventual goal to let them operate devices without keyboards or other physical controls.

Neuralink said patients with ALS may be eligible for the LINK trial, but it didn't specify other requirements or the number of participants. It now has approval recruit participants, then conduct the study under an approved clinical protocol. If the technology proves to be safe, the trial may allow Neuralink to apply for more advanced trials and eventually release LINK onto the market.

articles.headline: Pritzker accused of turning education tax credit into partisan fight by opting out of program: 'Sad to see'
keyFacts: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker opted out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, prompting criticism from education advocacy groups.
Pritzker stated the program siphons public education money, while advocate Sydney Altfield said it will cost Illinois families $2 billion.
Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield expressed hope that more Democratic governors will opt into the program before January 1.
body: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker , a Democrat, is being accused of putting partisan politics over kids' educational needs after he decided to opt out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, prompting criticism from parents and education advocacy groups.

Pritzker announced on Tuesday that his state will not opt into the program, which was signed into law by President Donald Trump last year as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The governor described the program as a school voucher, while advocacy groups argued that he mischaracterized the plan.

"At a time when public school education needs investments more than ever, we should not siphon money from public schools for private education – especially as the Trump Administration's policies decimate education," Pritzker said in a statement. "We have a responsibility to do right by all of our students. Taxpayer funding should not subsidize donations to private schools that could discriminate based on religion, sexual orientation, or other characteristics."

The program allows people to receive federal tax credits for donations up to $1,700 to authorized scholarship-granting organizations (SGOs), which distribute the donated scholarship funds to eligible families to be used on private or public educational expenses, including private school tuition, tutoring services, textbooks and more.
GOV HOCHUL'S PLAN TO OPT NEW YORK INTO FEDERAL SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM DRAWS UNION OPPOSITION
In an interview with Fox News Digital, Teach Coalition CEO Sydney Altfield said her advocacy group is "extremely disappointed" in the governor for opting out of the program.

"Not only did he opt kids out of his state and families out of his state from receiving scholarships, but the program allows for Illinois residents to still claim the tax credit. And what that means is that money that should have and could have gone to students and families in Illinois will now just move over the border and flow out of state — over about $2 billion in estimated scholarship money that could have stayed in the state," she explained.

Pritzker said in his announcement that his opt-out reaffirms his commitment to strengthening the state’s public schools by ensuring federal taxpayer resources remain available to the students and communities they are intended to serve. ​
But Altfield took issue with Pritzker describing the program as a voucher, contending that it does not take money from public schools.

"In the same vein of him opting out, he completely misrepresented this program, saying that it is a voucher scheme. It is by definition not a voucher. It does not take a dollar from [the] public school systems. All it does is incentivize taxpayers to use their tax dollars, their federal tax dollars, not their state tax dollars, but federal tax dollars for scholarship money. And instead of it helping families in Illinois, it will now help families outside," Altfield said.
TRUMP EDUCATION OFFICIAL SAYS SCHOOL CHOICE PROGRAM WILL PUT PRESSURE ON DEM-LED STATES

"Public school students are able to take this money," she added. "And we know that the vast majority of Illinois students go to public schools. That means the vast majority of taxpayers in the state send their kids to public schools. So we will see the vast majority of taxpayers designating their tax dollars to help support SGOs that will, in turn, support public school kids and students."
Altfield also accused Pritzker of putting children in the crossfire of partisan politics over an issue that she believes has an opportunity for a rare showing of bipartisanship.

Three other Democrats — Colorado Gov. Jared Polis, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul and New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham — joined dozens of Republicans in opting their states into the program. However, some states that have already opted in will have a new Democratic governor in January, such as Colorado, where Gov.-elect Phil Weiser has already signaled plans to withdraw.
Kansas, Kentucky and North Carolina all have Democratic governors who did not want to join the program, but GOP legislatures in those states overrode the governors' vetoes.

"I think it's really sad to see — to put kids in the middle of partisan politics," Altfield said of Pritzker's opt-out. "Many blue state governors — Gov. Hochul, Gov. Polis in Colorado and the New Mexico governor — have put politics aside and have put kids first. And I think that if governors can peel back whatever misconceptions they are reading and they can read the program for what it is, it is bipartisan. It will have bipartisan support because education, kids, families are the ones that are going to be successful in this."
"I think we're going to see, and I hope we're going to see, more Democratic governors opting into this program before Jan. 1," she added.
Altfield also noted that the program could benefit families who may be struggling financially amid concerns in Illinois and across the nation about affordability.

"We all know that affordability is the number one issue that Democrats and everyone is running on and everyone is feeling a pinch of the penny across the country. And this is a real opportunity that has money flowing into the state of Illinois that could have helped families that are pinching every dollar. For the working mom of two or three or four, she may have one or two jobs, three jobs. Where is she sending her kid after school? Is she paying for after-school care? The tax credit program could have offered her a scholarship to help cover those costs," Altfield said.

"We talk about teachers paying out of pocket. It's been estimated that teachers pay well over $800 out of their pocket for school supplies. Imagine if every low-income kid came to school with all of the school supplies needed. That teacher would not have to pay out of pocket. It's small things like this that really add up in a pocketbook that are now not available to the families and the students in Illinois," she continued.

After crawling inside the warehouse, walk to the far end and turn right to enter the glowing red room. Go a little farther to find the, uh, "trophies," and inspect all three lockers, along with the missing persons posters on the wall. This is where you begin your hunt for Gellhorn's three missing tourists.
- The images are saved as "Creepy Photos" in your phone gallery
- Refer to the pictures to find three locations around Gellhorn
- Your phone reminds you to look around when you're close to one of the spots
- Call the Kelly County Tip Line after every discovery
I've got all three locations highlighted below, but if you want to solve it yourself, now is the time to turn back.
All three missing persons locations

- Patrick Murray is in an abandoned trailer park just north of a water tower. It's the northernmost location in the Missing Persons case, and it's impossible to miss if you head west from Hank's Waffles toward the beach.
- Susanne Keeble is in the junkyard, across the street from a drive-in theatre and beside the Pay 'n' Spray off of Gellhorn Ave.
- Donald Miller is in a Borrachero Sound inlet, southeast of the hangar at Wild Hog Point. Look for a submerged car when you're in the area.
How to find Patrick Murray

The first missing person in northwest Gellhorn is in an abandoned trailer—the water tower's shadow is your giveaway. Run along the fence and enter the blue building from the back. There's an awfully suspicious hole in the floor, so pull the remaining floorboards back to discover what's left of Patrick Murray.
Call the Kelly County Tip Line after you find Patrick's remains and leave a message. No one will answer the phone, for now.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
How to find Susanne Keeble

The second missing person is in the junkyard, inside the trunk of an old pink DeVanity. The junkyard is right beside Pay 'n' Spray off Gellhorn Ave, across the street from the drive-in theatre. You'll spot Susanne Keeble's pink car with the PRTYGRL license plate while facing the drive-in.

After finding a second body, call the tip line again to finally speak to an investigator. They're thrilled to hear there's renewed interest in the case, and ask that you keep in contact should you make any further discoveries.
How to find Donald Miller

The third missing person is in a U-shaped inlet off the Borrachero Sound. You can find the smaller body of water by traveling southeast from the Wild Hog Point hangar. The view of Wild Hog Point from the tree in the creepy photo is your giveaway, so start looking for a submerged car when you find the right perspective.
After finding a third body, the investigator from the tip line asks to meet in the abandoned warehouse. And no, it's not just you, it's a pretty shady proposition.
Find the Port Gellhorn Serial Killer

When you're ready for the meeting, consider whether you want to go with your partner or go alone. Both seem to give me the same boost to Jason and Lucia's relationship status, elevating it to Hot Together (4/4) status for the first time in Chapter 2. It had dropped all the way down to Partners in Crime (2/4) just before this, so the Missing Persons quest was a much-appreciated bump.

You can also get the serial killer's glasses from his body if you choose to continue as a couple. They're beyond creepy, so I wouldn't blame you if you left them there, but aside from that, there's no cash reward. You will have to do it, though, if you're going for a 100% GTA 6 run.
Return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room alone

As either Jason or Lucia, return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room and meet Alvan West—the man you spoke to on the Kelly County Tips Line. He's got a 'surprise' waiting for you in the fourth locker, and a fight ensues after checking it out.

Going alone means there's no one there to save the passed out Jason or Lucia, and the serial killer takes them to a cave in Lummox County. The attack automatically triggers a character swap, leaving you to investigate your partner's whereabouts after receiving suspicious texts.
- Head to the waypoint marking the mine in Lummox County
- Enter the mine and follow the lights to free your partner
- Alvan will attack the couple with an axe a few times
- Chase him to the dead end and shoot him to stop his next lethal attack
Return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room together

Enter the abandoned warehouse trophy room just like before while your partner waits outside. When they sense something is off, they'll run inside to save you just as you pass out. After Alvan is dead, inspect his body—you can take his glasses as a souvenir. That's freak behavior, but I'm not judging. We gotta get that 100% cosmetic collection somehow.
